title: Ibrahim asked his guests why they had really come.
subtitle: A good host asks the real question

key.label: What he did with the moment

row.title: take the good news and rest

then: The angels had just given Ibrahim the news of a son. His fear was gone. Instead of only enjoying the moment, {idea}he asked what their real mission was.{/idea} The tafsir links this to how he then pleaded for the people of Lut.
now: You get the promotion, the good test result, the yes you wanted. The easy thing is to close the door and celebrate. {idea}Ibrahim's question was about other people.{/idea} Who else is going through something right now?
old: When good news comes, my day is done.
new: Good news for me can open my eyes to what others are facing.
try: After your next bit of good news, message one person who is struggling and ask how they are.

title: The same visitors carried joy for one, warning for another.
subtitle: The mission to the people of Lut
then: The angels answered Ibrahim plainly. They were sent to {trap}a people who were criminals{/trap}, the people of Lut. The same guests who brought Ibrahim glad news carried a very different message to the next town.
now: Two coworkers get called into the same office on the same morning. One leaves smiling, one leaves shaken. {idea}The meeting did not decide that. What came before it did.{/idea}
old: What happens to people is mostly random.
new: Often what reaches us carries the shape of what we did before it came.
try: Think of one habit you would not want to be called in about. Start changing it today, quietly.

title: Stones of clay, sent with purpose.
subtitle: The form the punishment would take
then: The angels named exactly what they carried: {trap}stones of baked clay{/trap} for a people who would not stop. The tafsir calls them stones of sijjil. It was not chance. It was sent.
now: You read about a collapse, a scandal, a ruin, and call it bad luck. Some endings are, but some are the slow result of years of warnings ignored. {idea}The verse asks you to read your own warnings while they are still warnings.{/idea}
new: Some consequences are answers, and warnings come long before them.
try: Name one warning you have been getting lately, from your body, your family, or your conscience. Write it down.

title: Each stone was marked with its owner's name.
subtitle: Nothing aimed at random
then: The stones were {idea}marked in the presence of your Lord{/idea}. The tafsir says they were recorded with Allah to their names: {trap}each stone has the name of its companion.{/trap} The ones who went too far were known one by one.
now: You tell yourself you are one of millions, one comment in a thread, one face at the party. No one will notice what you did. {idea}You are not a number to Allah.{/idea} Your name is known, and so is every small good you do.
old: In a crowd, what I do disappears.
new: Allah knows me by name, so nothing I do is anonymous.
try: Do one good thing today that no one will see or thank you for.

title: Before the stones fell, the believers were brought out.
subtitle: Rescue came first

row.title: the good die with the bad

then: Ibrahim had worried: Lut is in that town. The tafsir quotes the angels' reply, {idea}we know better who is there.{/idea} So the believers, Lut and his family except his wife, {reward}were brought out first.{/reward}
now: You worry about your children in a hard school, your friend in a toxic workplace, yourself in a city that pulls you the wrong way. {idea}Allah sees who is who inside the crowd.{/idea} Keep your faith, and trust that you are not lost in it.
old: If I live around wrong, I will be swept away with it.
new: Allah knows exactly who holds on, even in the middle of a bad place.
try: Make one dua today for someone you love who lives somewhere hard.

title: In a whole town, only one household held on.
subtitle: Being the one house
then: When the town was searched, {reward}only one household of Muslims{/reward} was found: Lut's family. Even inside it, his wife stayed behind, as the tafsir notes. {trap}The rest of the town had turned away.{/trap}
now: The office where everyone pads expenses. The friend group where everyone mocks the same person. The family where no one prays. {idea}You can be the one house.{/idea} It feels lonely, and it is seen.
old: If everyone around me does it, it cannot be that bad.
new: Allah looks at each house, not at the average of the street.
try: Pick one small thing you do differently from your circle for Allah's sake, and keep doing it today.

title: The ruins were left as a sign for those who fear.
subtitle: Who actually learns from a ruin

key.label: Two ways to pass a ruin

row.title: a mirror
sub: what does this say to me

then: Allah left {trap}a proof of the punishment{/trap} in that place. The tafsir says their dwellings became a putrid, dead sea. {idea}It is a lesson for the believers{/idea}, but only those who fear will read it.
now: You scroll past a story of a family torn apart by one secret, a career ended by one habit. Most people say how sad and keep scrolling. {idea}The person who fears asks: is any of that in me?{/idea}
old: Other people's downfalls are just stories.
new: A ruin is a message, but only to the one who is willing to be warned.
try: Next time you hear of someone's downfall, ask one honest question about yourself before you comment.

title: Musa came to Pharaoh with proof that was plain.
subtitle: The next sign: clear authority
then: After Lut's town, the surah turns to Musa. He was sent to Pharaoh {idea}with a manifest authority{/idea}, which the tafsir explains as clear proof and plain evidence. The problem would never be the proof.
now: You say you would change if you were sure. Then the doctor shows you the scan, the bank shows you the numbers, a friend shows you the pattern. {trap}Still you wait.{/trap} Sometimes the proof is already on the table.
old: I will change once I am completely convinced.
new: Clear proof often arrives early. What is missing is the will to accept it.
try: Name one thing you already know is true but keep asking for more proof about. Act on it in one small way.

title: Pharaoh turned his back and called the messenger names.
subtitle: Labels as a way to avoid the message
then: Pharaoh {trap}turned away in rebellion and arrogance{/trap}, leaning on his supporters. He did not answer Musa's proof. He picked a label: a sorcerer or a madman. The tafsir ties this to bending the neck in pride.
now: Someone points out something true about you and you reply, she is just jealous, he is so dramatic. {trap}The label ends the conversation.{/trap} {idea}It does not end the truth.{/idea}
old: If I can label the critic, I can ignore the criticism.
new: Attacking the messenger is a way of running from the message.
try: Recall one criticism you dismissed by labeling the person. Look at the criticism alone for a minute.

title: The army that backed him sank with him.
subtitle: What his supporters were worth
then: Pharaoh had turned away {reward}with his supporters{/reward}. Now Allah took him and his armies and threw them into the sea. The tafsir says he was {trap}a denying sinner worthy of blame.{/trap}
now: You feel safe because your people are with you: the team, the followers, the family that always takes your side. {idea}Backing is not the same as being right.{/idea} The people who agree with you cannot carry your blame for you.
old: With enough people on my side, I am safe.
new: Support from people does not protect me from being wrong.
try: Ask one person who usually disagrees with you for their honest view on something you are doing.

title: A wind that brought nothing, sent against Aad.
subtitle: The barren wind

row.title: rain carrier
sub: the winds at the surah's start

row.title: barren
sub: the same air, turned against them

then: The surah opened by swearing by winds that scatter and carry rain. Here is the other kind: {trap}the barren wind{/trap} sent against Aad. The tafsir says it destroys everything and {trap}produces nothing{/trap}.
now: The same phone that connects you to family can empty your evenings. The same money that feeds your house can fill it with arguments. {idea}What blesses or harms is in Allah's hand.{/idea} The thing itself is not your safety.
old: The things that serve me will always serve me.
new: The same gift can become a trial. My safety is with Allah, not with things.
try: Pick one thing you rely on daily and say a short thanks to Allah for it before using it.

title: Whatever the wind touched turned to dust.
subtitle: How complete the end was
then: The wind {trap}spared nothing that it reached{/trap}. The tafsir says it made everything like something rotten and destroyed. Aad had been known for their strength and their buildings. None of it held.
now: You spend years on the house, the follower count, the business name. A fire, a market crash, one bad night can flatten it. {idea}What is done for Allah does not crumble that way.{/idea}
old: If I build it strong enough, it will last.
new: Everything I build can fall. What I do for Allah is what remains.
try: Give a little of your time or money today to something that will outlast you.

title: Thamud were told: enjoy yourselves, but only for a while.
subtitle: A deadline given as a warning
then: Thamud were {trap}guided but preferred blindness{/trap}, as the tafsir quotes from another surah. Then they were told to enjoy themselves for a while. The tafsir says they were given three days before the torment came.
now: The free trial ends Friday. The warning letter says thirty days. You treat the gap as more time to relax. {idea}Every respite is a chance to turn around{/idea}, and your life itself is one.
old: Extra time means I can keep going as I am.
new: Extra time is a gift to change, not a pause before nothing.
try: Think of one thing you keep putting off making right. Do the first step before tomorrow.

title: They defied the command, and it hit them while watching.
subtitle: Seeing it coming is not escaping it
then: Thamud {trap}insolently defied the command of their Lord{/trap}. The tafsir says that on the early morning of the fourth day, the blast seized them. {trap}They were looking right at it.{/trap}
now: You watch your health slip, your marriage cool, your prayers thin out. You notice every sign. {idea}Noticing is not the same as turning.{/idea} Knowing a problem is coming does not stop it.
old: As long as I am aware of a problem, I have it under control.
new: Awareness without turning back changes nothing.
try: Take one problem you have been just watching and do one real thing about it today.

title: They could not stand, and no one could help.
subtitle: When all strength runs out
then: When the blast came, Thamud {trap}were unable to rise up{/trap}. The tafsir says they could not run from it, {trap}nor save themselves{/trap}. The strength they were proud of was gone in one moment.
now: Lying in a hospital bed, you learn how little you control. You cannot stand up alone, and the people you counted on can only wait in the corridor. {idea}The time to lean on Allah is now, while you can still stand.{/idea}
old: I can always rely on myself when things get bad.
new: My strength can vanish in a moment. Allah is the help that remains.
try: Stand up from where you are, and say one honest dua asking Allah for help with something you carry.
